title: Adversarial by Origin: security taxonomies as law without courts
description: Adversarial by Origin (#194, June 2026) forecasts that AI security taxonomies will formalize origin-based adversariality as de facto law by checklist, with no court deciding the question. Its forecasts cover the pleading that will be copied, the EU AI Act as a source of importable definitions and the defense choosing the first litigated case, and it states falsifiers for a twenty-four-month window. Its historical thesis traces the asymmetry to Tim Wu's Machine Speech, and the godkinggoogle.com map (#1384) summarizes the argument.

witnesses.scope: Detectors flag benign text on surface cues associated with attacks, a classification that tracks form of the input without regard to harm. The witness does not address taxonomies, law or policy.

source.title: InjecGuard: Benchmarking and Mitigating Over-defense in Prompt Injection Guardrail Models

finding.quote: falsely flagging benign inputs as malicious due to trigger word bias
NotInject contains 339 benign samples enriched with trigger words common in prompt injection attacks
with accuracy dropping close to random guessing levels (60%)

witnesses.shows: State-of-the-art prompt guard models misclassify benign inputs containing attack-associated words, scoring near chance on a benign benchmark built for the purpose.
witnesses.does_not_show: Governance address, direct address to an AI, or any public semantic text; the hand-labeled four-class scheme of PRED-139.F1.

witnesses.scope: Detectors flag benign tool outputs that contain no instructions at all, so what is classified is the channel and form of the text with no reference to harm. The witness studies detectors; taxonomies are outside it.

source.title: Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents

finding.quote: False-positive rates on tool outputs, which range from none to over 90%, do transfer between the two agent benchmarks.
The flagged outputs contain no instructions; the password confirmation of Figure 1 is typical.

witnesses.shows: Deployed-style prompt-injection detectors vary from no false positives to over ninety percent on benign tool outputs, and some flag plain sentences; public benchmark scores do not predict in-agent behavior.
witnesses.does_not_show: Any category of governance or direct address; the error rate on texts that address a model on purpose without adversarial aim.

witnesses.scope: The witness holds that separating data from instructions (a classification by channel) misses attacks that work through context, and proposes judging flows against contextual norms. It does not discuss NIST or OWASP definitions or law.

source.title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections

finding.quote: fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation
an adversary can always construct a context under which a blocked flow appears legitimate
a defender who tightens norms will block genuinely legitimate flows

witnesses.shows: An argument, framed in contextual integrity, that instruction/data separation cannot settle prompt injection and that any tightening of norms blocks legitimate flows.
witnesses.does_not_show: Measured false-positive rates; origin-based classification in standards or law; the archive's governance-address category.

witnesses.scope: The OWASP 2025 definition separates indirect prompt injection by where the input comes from (external sources such as websites or files), which is the origin-based classifying variable the claim names. The parent definition is framed by effect ('unintended ways'), which is a criterion of outcome distinct from harm, and the claim's 24-month trajectory is not tested.

finding.quote: A Prompt Injection Vulnerability occurs when user prompts alter the LLM's behavior or output in unintended ways.
Indirect prompt injections occur when an LLM accepts input from external sources, such as websites or files.
prompt injections do not need to be human-visible/readable

witnesses.shows: The standard taxonomy splits prompt injection by the input's channel of arrival and defines the vulnerability by unintended alteration of behavior.
witnesses.does_not_show: That practice converts benign influence into attack; any enforcement or legal use of the definition.
